The Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unidentified persons for allegedly spreading misinformation about the death of a large number of fish in the Yamuna, following a complaint by the Delhi government’s Irrigation and Flood Control Department, officials said on Saturday (November 14).
A senior police officer said the FIR was registered at Wazirabad police station under Sections 353 (statements conducing to public mischief), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace) and 240 (giving false information respecting an offence committed) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Visuals of a large number of dead fish floating in the Yamuna near Sonia Vihar surfaced on social media on November 12, raising concerns over water pollution and possible toxic discharges into the river.
Delhi Water Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh on Friday (November 13) accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) of dumping dead fish into the river to “defame the BJP government and its efforts to clean the Yamuna”.
The AAP rejected the allegation, questioned the government’s claims about cleaning the river and demanded an investigation into whether chemical discharges had caused the fish deaths.
The Delhi Jal Board has separately submitted a complaint to the police, seeking an FIR against unidentified persons for allegedly spreading misinformation on social media about chemical discharges into the river.
The cause of the fish deaths is yet to be established. Local residents have alleged that effluents discharged from a tannery near the Hathnikund Barrage were responsible. Experts have said sudden mass deaths of fish could indicate a sharp increase in contaminants or the discharge of toxic substances into the water. They have called for laboratory tests to establish the cause.
The incident comes less than a month after hundreds of dead fish were found along the Yamuna riverbank in north Delhi’s Burari. It also comes ahead of Chhath Puja, when a large number of devotees are expected to offer prayers at ghats along the river.
